text:
maya: Quick heads-up — OKR sync for Private deployments. Need to lock Q3 roadmap by EOD Fri. Main pillars: VPC control plane parity, on‑prem packaging/installer, and air‑gapped validation + docs. A few pilot customers are pushing for different combos (bank, med-device, gov). Please review proposed priority and launch criteria below and drop reactions/comments.

maya: Proposed priorities (ranked):
1) VPC control plane parity (networking, routing, policy hooks) — must for early enterprise wins
2) On‑prem packaging & one-click installer (k8s+baremetal artifacts) — medium risk but high adoption
3) Air‑gapped validation & documented test harness — required for gov/regulated customers
4) KMS/HSM integrations + audit streaming — must for security review, but can be parallel work

maya: Quick ask: engineering estimates, security blockers, and what minimum GA criteria look like for each. If you disagree with ordering, say so and propose tradeoffs.

ashish: Re VPC parity — big chunk is control-plane networking (route tables, private endpoints). Also need to finish policy engine work (PRs in review). Rough effort: 6w for core, +2w for canary infra.

ashish: On‑prem packaging — we can reuse parts of dedicated infra, but we'll need to stabilize container images + packaging scripts. I'd budget 4w for MVP packaging + 2w for installer UX.

lina: For on‑prem/offline mode we need to define model artifact formats. If customers want quantized floats we need CI for conversion and QA. Est: 3w to build conversion pipeline and tests.

sam: Security concerns: air‑gapped == no external telemetry. We need a policy for offline telemetry opt-out, signed release artifacts, and reproducible builds. Also HSM/KMS requirements — will require integration + penetration test. Can't ship GA without signed artifacts.

sam: Also must confirm supply-chain policy for on‑prem images (SBOM + image signing).

joel: Sales input: Bank customer (Pilot A) will only move if VPC control plane supports private endpoints + per-tenant routing. They can commit to a paid pilot if we can guarantee network isolation. Gov prospect needs air‑gap proof. They'll pay for on‑prem packaging as professional services if needed.

joel: Prioritization wise — VPC parity unlocks immediate revenue. On‑prem packaging sells too but can be PS-heavy initially.

harper: Solutions note: For installer, we should support two modes: 'managed' (control plane in customer VPC, Redwood control plane endpoints) and 'air‑gapped' (fully offline installer + local console). That matches asks and reduces scope for first GA (start with managed + offline docs).

harper: Quick config sample for installer (MVP):
```yaml
installer:
  mode: managed  # managed | airgap
  network:
    use_private_endpoint: true
    allowed_cidr: ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  storage:
    backend: nfs
  kms:
    type: optional
```

zoe: From CS — pilots want a deterministic test plan: perf baseline (p50/p95), failover test, upgrade test, and security checklist. If we provide a runnable harness they can validate on their infra.

maya: Launch criteria draft (please thumbs up / comment):
- VPC control plane: private endpoint, routing rules, policy hooks, e2e tests in staging
- On‑prem pack: container images + installer, basic upgrade path, SBOM and signed artifacts
- Air‑gapped: docs + validation harness for offline install, telemetry opt-out, signed bundles
- Security: KMS/HSM integration documented (can be alpha), SBOM + supply-chain controls in place
- Pilot acceptance: at least one paid pilot for each major vertical (bank, gov, healthcare)

ashish: Technical risk callout: if we need to support legacy k8s (<1.22) for some customers, installer complexity goes up. Suggest we define a supported k8s matrix for GA and treat older versions as PS.

lina: Model-related risk: quantization/regression testing needs to be part of the pipeline — otherwise customers will surface quality drift. We should include a small regen test set in the installer validation.

sam: One compliance note — gov customers sometimes require yearly CTI scans. Add that to enterprise onboarding checklist.

joel: Can we get a clear list of must-have vs nice-to-have for the sales contract? I can negotiate if we know what to promise. My advice: promise VPC parity + signed images; list air‑gapped support as "coming soon" with a defined timeline.

maya: Good suggestion. I'll convert launch criteria into must/nice lists and post an updated doc.

harper: For docs: need quickstart + troubleshooting + upgrade notes. Also include 'how to validate network isolation' guide for security teams.

deploy-bot: New ticket created: PRIV-341 "Private: onprem installer MVP" assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/PRIV-341

maya: Next steps: engineers — drop estimates in the ticket by EOD tomorrow. Security — list blockers and must-have gating items. Sales/CS — prioritize pilot list and sign commitments. I'll collate into a single roadmap and share with execs on Friday.

ashish: Will add estimates.

sam: I'll enumerate gating items and add to PRIV-341.

joel: I'll try to lock bank pilot terms this week.

zoe: I'll prep the validation harness template.

maya: Thanks — please add brief notes inline in thread for any disagreements. :thumbsup:

harper: +1

lina: +1

ashish: +1

sam: noted

joel: got it

maya: If anyone needs 1:1 to sync, ping me.
